sanskrit: duryodhaneyaṃ cintā me śaśvan nāpy upaśāmyati satyaṃ hy etad ahaṃ manye pratyakṣaṃ nānumānataḥ
english: O Duryodhana, this anxiety of mine never ceases; I believe this to be truly self-evident, not merely inferred.

sanskrit: ātmajeṣu paraṃ snehaṃ sarvabhūtāni kurvate priyāṇi caiṣāṃ kurvanti yathāśakti hitāni ca
english: All beings cherish supreme love for their own offspring, and they do whatever is pleasing and beneficial to them according to their ability.

sanskrit: evam evopakartṝṇāṃ prāyaśo lakṣayāmahe icchanti bahulaṃ santaḥ pratikartuṃ mahat priyam
english: In the same way, we observe that those who receive help from benefactors generally wish greatly to repay them with something highly pleasing.

sanskrit: agniḥ sācivyakartā syāt khāṇḍave tat kṛtaṃ smaran arjunasyātibhīme 'smin kurupāṇḍusamāgame
english: Agni, remembering what was done for him in the Khāṇḍava forest, may become an ally of Arjuna in this most dreadful clash between the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: jātagṛdhyābhipannāś ca pāṇḍavānām anekaśaḥ dharmādayo bhaviṣyanti samāhūtā divaukasaḥ
english: And the celestial beings, led by Dharma himself, who have become greatly devoted to the Pāṇḍavas, will come in many ways when summoned.

sanskrit: bhīṣmadroṇakṛpādīnāṃ bhayād aśanisaṃmitam rirakṣiṣantaḥ saṃrambhaṃ gamiṣyantīti me matiḥ
english: My conviction is that the gods, wishing to protect them, will rise up in fury equal to the thunderbolt, out of fear of Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Kṛpa, and others.

sanskrit: te devasahitāḥ pārthā na śakyāḥ prativīkṣitum mānuṣeṇa naravyāghrā vīryavanto 'strapāragāḥ
english: The sons of Pāṇḍu, those tigers among men, mighty and masters of weaponry, aided by the gods, cannot be withstood even by glance of a mortal.

sanskrit: durāsadaṃ yasya divyaṃ gāṇḍīvaṃ dhanur uttamam vāruṇau cākṣayau divyau śarapūrṇau maheṣudhī
english: He whose divine bow Gāṇḍīva is unapproachable, that supreme weapon; and whose two divine inexhaustible quivers full of arrows, gifts of Varuṇa, are vast treasuries of shafts—

sanskrit: vānaraś ca dhvajo divyo niḥsaṅgo dhūmavad gatiḥ rathaś ca caturantāyāṃ yasya nāsti samas tviṣā
english: Whose divine banner bears the monkey and moves swift as smoke, unimpeded; whose chariot has no equal in splendor in the four-cornered earth—

sanskrit: mahāmeghanibhaś cāpi nirghoṣaḥ śrūyate janaiḥ mahāśanisamaḥ śabdaḥ śātravāṇāṃ bhayaṃkaraḥ
english: The rumble of whose chariot is heard by men like the roar of great clouds, and whose sound, comparable to a great thunderbolt, is terrifying to his enemies—

sanskrit: yaṃ cātimānuṣaṃ vīrye kṛtsno loko vyavasyati devānām api jetāraṃ yaṃ viduḥ pārthivā raṇe
english: Him whom the entire world judges to possess superhuman valor, whom the kings know in battle as one who can conquer even the gods—

sanskrit: śatāni pañca caiveṣūn udvapann iva dṛśyate nimeṣāntaramātreṇa muñcan dūraṃ ca pātayan
english: Who appears as if tossing five hundred arrows in an instant, releasing them in the mere twinkling of an eye and sending them flying far—

sanskrit: yam āha bhīṣmo droṇaś ca kṛpo drauṇis tathaiva ca madrarājas tathā śalyo madhyasthā ye ca mānavāḥ
english: Of whom Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Kṛpa, Droṇa's son Aśvatthāmā, the king of Madra Śalya, and all neutral men have spoken—

sanskrit: yuddhāyāvasthitaṃ pārthaṃ pārthivair atimānuṣaiḥ aśakyaṃ rathaśārdūlaṃ parājetum ariṃdamam
english: That subduer of enemies, Pārtha, tiger among chariot warriors, standing ready for battle, cannot be defeated by kings even with superhuman effort.

sanskrit: kṣipaty ekena vegena pañca bāṇaśatāni yaḥ sadṛśaṃ bāhuvīryeṇa kārtavīryasya pāṇḍavam
english: That son of Pāṇḍu, who launches five hundred arrows in a single burst, is equal in the strength of his arms to Kārtavīrya himself.

sanskrit: tam arjunaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ mahendropendrarakṣitam nighnantam iva paśyāmi vimarde 'smin mahāmṛdhe
english: In this great and terrible conflict, I see that great bowman Arjuna, protected by Mahendra and Upendra, striking down enemies as it were.

sanskrit: ity evaṃ cintayan kṛtsnam ahorātrāṇi bhārata anidro niḥsukhaś cāsmi kurūṇāṃ śamacintayā
english: Thus reflecting upon all of this day and night, O Bhārata, I am sleepless and joyless, consumed by thoughts of peace for the Kurus.

sanskrit: kṣayodayo 'yaṃ sumahān kurūṇāṃ pratyupasthitaḥ asya cet kalahasyāntaḥ śamād anyo na vidyate
english: A very great rise and fall of the Kurus is at hand; and for this conflict there is no end other than peace.

sanskrit: śamo me rocate nityaṃ pārthais tāta na vigrahaḥ kurubhyo hi sadā manye pāṇḍavāñ śaktimattarān
english: Peace with the Pāṇḍavas always pleases me, my son, not conflict; for I always believe the Pāṇḍavas to be more powerful than the Kurus.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca pitur etad vacaḥ śrutvā dhārtarāṣṭro 'tyamarṣaṇaḥ ādhāya vipulaṃ krodhaṃ punar evedam abravīt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard his father's words, Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, exceedingly wrathful, harboring immense anger, spoke again thus:

sanskrit: aśakyā devasacivāḥ pārthāḥ syur iti yad bhavān manyate tadbhayaṃ vyetu bhavato rājasattama
english: O best of kings, let that fear of yours depart — that fear in which you think the Pāṇḍavas would be aided by the gods and thus impossible to overcome.

sanskrit: akāmadveṣasaṃyogād drohāl lobhāc ca bhārata upekṣayā ca bhāvānāṃ devā devatvam āpnuvan
english: O Bhārata, the gods attained their divine status by freedom from desire and hatred, by abstaining from treachery and greed, and by equanimity in their dispositions.

sanskrit: iti dvaipāyano vyāso nāradaś ca mahātapāḥ jāmadagnyaś ca rāmo naḥ kathām akathayat purā
english: Thus Dvaipāyana Vyāsa, and Nārada the great ascetic, and Rāma the son of Jamadagni once told us this teaching.

sanskrit: naiva mānuṣavad devāḥ pravartante kadā cana kāmāl lobhād anukrośād dveṣāc ca bharatarṣabha
english: The gods never act as humans do — out of desire, greed, compassion, or hatred, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: yadi hy agniś ca vāyuś ca dharma indro 'śvināv api kāmayogāt pravarteran na pārthā duḥkham āpnuyuḥ
english: For if Agni, Vāyu, Dharma, Indra, and the two Aśvins were to act out of passionate attachment, the Pāṇḍavas would not have suffered as they did.

sanskrit: tasmān na bhavatā cintā kāryaiṣā syāt kadā cana daiveṣv apekṣakā hy ete śaśvad bhāveṣu bhārata
english: Therefore you should never worry about this, O Bhārata; for these gods are always evenhanded in their regard for all things.

sanskrit: atha cet kāmasaṃyogād dveṣāl lobhāc ca lakṣyate deveṣu devaprāmāṇyaṃ naiva tad vikramiṣyati
english: But if divine authority were seen in the gods to stem from desire, hatred, or greed, it would never hold sway.

sanskrit: mayābhimantritaḥ śaśvaj jātavedāḥ praśaṃsati didhakṣuḥ sakalāṃl lokān parikṣipya samantataḥ
english: Agni, the knower of all things born, whom I have always energized with my mantras, ever blazes with the desire to burn all the worlds, encircling them on all sides.

sanskrit: yad vā paramakaṃ tejo yena yuktā divaukasaḥ mamāpy anupamaṃ bhūyo devebhyo viddhi bhārata
english: Whatever supreme energy the celestial beings possess — know, O Bhārata, that I have an energy beyond theirs, incomparable and surpassing.

sanskrit: pradīryamāṇāṃ vasudhāṃ girīṇāṃ śikharāṇi ca lokasya paśyato rājan sthāpayāmy abhimantraṇāt
english: O king, when the earth is splitting apart and the peaks of mountains are crumbling, I stabilize them through my incantations, even as the world watches.

sanskrit: cetanācetanasyāsya jaṅgamasthāvarasya ca vināśāya samutpannaṃ mahāghoraṃ mahāsvanam
english: Whatever terrifying, immense sound arises for the destruction of moving and non-moving, conscious and unconscious beings—

sanskrit: aśmavarṣaṃ ca vāyuṃ ca śamayāmīha nityaśaḥ jagataḥ paśyato 'bhīkṣṇaṃ bhūtānām anukampayā
english: —showers of stones and violent winds I always calm here, even as the world beholds it, out of compassion for all creatures.

sanskrit: stambhitāsv apsu gacchanti mayā rathapadātayaḥ devāsurāṇāṃ bhāvānām aham ekaḥ pravartitā
english: Chariots and foot soldiers march over waters that I have made solid; I alone set in motion the course of both the gods and the asuras.

sanskrit: akṣauhiṇībhir yān deśān yāmi kāryeṇa kena cit tatrāpo me pravartante yatra yatrābhikāmaye
english: In whatever regions I march with akshauhini armies for some purpose, water flows wherever I desire.

sanskrit: bhayāni viṣaye rājan vyālādīni na santi me mattaḥ suptāni bhūtāni na hiṃsanti bhayaṃkarāḥ
english: In my domain, O king, there are no terrors such as serpents; fearsome creatures do not harm those who sleep under my protection.

sanskrit: nikāmavarṣī parjanyo rājan viṣayavāsinām dharmiṣṭhāś ca prajāḥ sarvā ītayaś ca na santi me
english: O king, the rain clouds shower abundantly for those dwelling in my realm; all the people are virtuous; and there are no calamities in my domain.

sanskrit: aśvināv atha vāyvagnī marudbhiḥ saha vṛtrahā dharmaś caiva mayā dviṣṭān notsahante 'bhirakṣitum
english: The two Aśvins, Vāyu, Agni, the Maruts along with the slayer of Vṛtra, and Dharma himself do not venture to protect those I hate.

sanskrit: yadi hy ete samarthāḥ syur maddviṣas trātum ojasā na sma trayodaśa samāḥ pārthā duḥkham avāpnuyuḥ
english: For had they been capable of protecting those I hate by their power, the Pāṇḍavas would not have suffered for thirteen years.

sanskrit: naiva devā na gandharvā nāsurā na ca rākṣasāḥ śaktās trātuṃ mayā dviṣṭaṃ satyam etad bravīmi te
english: Neither the gods, nor the gandharvas, nor the asuras, nor the rakshasas are capable of saving one whom I hate — I tell you this truly.

sanskrit: yad abhidhyāmy ahaṃ śaśvac chubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham naitad vipannapūrvaṃ me mitreṣv ariṣu cobhayoḥ
english: Whatever I continually contemplate — whether auspicious or inauspicious — that has never failed for me regarding both friends and enemies alike.

sanskrit: bhaviṣyatīdam iti vā yad bravīmi paraṃtapa nānyathā bhūtapūrvaṃ tat satyavāg iti māṃ viduḥ
english: Whatever I declare saying 'this shall come to pass,' O scorcher of foes, that has never turned out otherwise — they know me as one who speaks truth.

sanskrit: lokasākṣikam etan me māhātmyaṃ dikṣu viśrutam āśvāsanārthaṃ bhavataḥ proktaṃ na ślāghayā nṛpa
english: This greatness of mine, witnessed by the world and renowned in all directions, has been spoken for your reassurance, O king, not out of boastfulness.

sanskrit: na hy ahaṃ ślāghano rājan bhūtapūrvaḥ kadā cana asad ācaritaṃ hy etad yad ātmānaṃ praśaṃsati
english: For I, O king, have never before been one to boast; indeed, it is improper conduct for one to praise oneself.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavāṃś caiva matsyāṃś ca pāñcālān kekayaiḥ saha sātyakiṃ vāsudevaṃ ca śrotāsi vijitān mayā
english: You shall hear of the Pāṇḍavas and the Matsyas and the Pāñcālas together with the Kekayas, and Sātyaki and Vāsudeva, conquered by me.

sanskrit: saritaḥ sāgaraṃ prāpya yathā naśyanti sarvaśaḥ tathaiva te vinaṅkṣyanti mām āsādya sahānvayāḥ
english: Just as rivers perish entirely upon reaching the ocean, so too shall they perish completely, together with their kinsmen, when they encounter me.

sanskrit: parā buddhiḥ paraṃ tejo vīryaṃ ca paramaṃ mayi parā vidyā paro yogo mama tebhyo viśiṣyate
english: Supreme intelligence, supreme energy, supreme heroic strength are in me; supreme knowledge and supreme discipline are mine, surpassing those of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: pitāmahaś ca droṇaś ca kṛpaḥ śalyaḥ śalas tathā astreṣu yat prajānanti sarvaṃ tan mayi vidyate
english: Whatever the grandsire Bhīṣma, Droṇa, Kṛpa, Śalya, and Śala know in the science of weapons — all of that resides in me.

sanskrit: ity uktvā saṃjayaṃ bhūyaḥ paryapṛcchata bhārata jñātvā yuyutsuḥ kāryāṇi prāptakālam ariṃdama
english: Having spoken thus, O Bhārata, O subduer of enemies, he who sought battle questioned Sañjaya again, wishing to know what tasks needed to be done at the right moment.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tathā tu pṛcchantam atīva pārthān; vaicitravīryaṃ tam acintayitvā uvāca karṇo dhṛtarāṣṭraputraṃ; praharṣayan saṃsadi kauravāṇām
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: But as that son of Vicitravīrya was thus eagerly inquiring about the Pāṇḍavas, Karṇa, disregarding him, spoke to the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, gladdening the assembly of the Kauravas.

sanskrit: mithyā pratijñāya mayā yad astraṃ; rāmād dhṛtaṃ brahmapuraṃ purastāt vijñāya tenāsmi tadaivam uktas; tavāntakāle 'pratibhāsyatīti
english: The divine weapon known as Brahmā's city, which I obtained from Rāma by making a false claim — knowing this, he told me even then: 'At your time of death it will fail you.'

sanskrit: mahāparādhe hy api saṃnatena; maharṣiṇāhaṃ guruṇā ca śaptaḥ śaktaḥ pradagdhuṃ hy api tigmatejāḥ; sasāgarām apy avaniṃ maharṣiḥ
english: Though I bowed humbly in my great transgression, the great seer and teacher cursed me — that great sage of blazing splendor who is capable of burning even the earth along with the ocean.

sanskrit: prasāditaṃ hy asya mayā mano 'bhūc; chuśrūṣayā svena ca pauruṣeṇa tatas tad astraṃ mama sāvaśeṣaṃ; tasmāt samartho 'smi mamaiṣa bhāraḥ
english: Yet his mind was appeased by my devoted service and my own heroic exertion; thus that weapon still remains available to me in some measure — therefore I am capable, and this is my responsibility.

sanskrit: nimeṣamātraṃ tam ṛṣiprasādam; avāpya pāñcālakarūṣamatsyān nihatya pārthāṃś ca saputrapautrāṃl; lokān ahaṃ śastrajitān prapatsye
english: Having obtained that grace of the sage even for an instant, I shall slay the Pāñcālas, the Karūṣas, the Matsyas, and the Pāṇḍavas together with their sons and grandsons, and I shall attain worlds conquered by the sword.

sanskrit: pitāmahas tiṣṭhatu te samīpe; droṇaś ca sarve ca narendramukhyāḥ yathāpradhānena balena yātvā; pārthān haniṣyāmi mamaiṣa bhāraḥ
english: Let the grandsire stand near you, and Droṇa and all the foremost kings — advancing with force in proper array, I shall slay the Pāṇḍavas; this is my burden.

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvāṇaṃ tam uvāca bhīṣmaḥ; kiṃ katthase kālaparītabuddhe na karṇa jānāsi yathā pradhāne; hate hatāḥ syur dhṛtarāṣṭraputrāḥ
english: Bhīṣma spoke to him who was boasting thus: 'Why do you boast, O Karṇa, whose intellect is seized by fate? Do you not know, Karṇa, that when the chief warrior is slain in battle, the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra would be slain too?'

sanskrit: yat khāṇḍavaṃ dāhayatā kṛtaṃ hi; kṛṣṇadvitīyena dhanaṃjayena śrutvaiva tat karma niyantum ātmā; śakyas tvayā vai saha bāndhavena
english: What Dhanañjaya, with Kṛṣṇa as his second, accomplished in burning the Khāṇḍava forest — upon merely hearing of that deed, you together with your kinsmen might have been able to restrain yourself.

sanskrit: yāṃ cāpi śaktiṃ tridaśādhipas te; dadau mahātmā bhagavān mahendraḥ bhasmīkṛtāṃ tāṃ patitāṃ viśīrṇāṃ; cakrāhatāṃ drakṣyasi keśavena
english: And that power weapon which the great-souled lord Mahendra, king of the thirty gods, gave you — you shall see it reduced to ashes, fallen and shattered, struck by Keśava's discus.

sanskrit: yas te śaraḥ sarpamukho vibhāti; sadāgryamālyair mahitaḥ prayatnāt sa pāṇḍuputrābhihataḥ śaraughaiḥ; saha tvayā yāsyati karṇa nāśam
english: And that serpent-headed arrow of yours which shines and is always honored with the finest garlands and kept with great care — struck by the Pāṇḍava's shafts, it shall go to destruction along with you, O Karṇa.

sanskrit: bāṇasya bhaumasya ca karṇa hantā; kirīṭinaṃ rakṣati vāsudevaḥ yas tvādṛśānāṃ ca garīyasāṃ ca; hantā ripūṇāṃ tumule pragāḍhe
english: O Karṇa, Vāsudeva protects Kirīṭī — the slayer of Bāṇa and Bhaumasura — he who is the slayer of enemies greater than even ones such as you in the thick of battle.

sanskrit: karṇa uvāca asaṃśayaṃ vṛṣṇipatir yathoktas; tathā ca bhūyaś ca tato mahātmā ahaṃ yad uktaḥ paruṣaṃ tu kiṃ cit; pitāmahas tasya phalaṃ śṛṇotu
english: Karṇa said: Without doubt, the lord of the Vṛṣṇis is as described — and even more, that great-souled one. But as for the harsh words the grandsire has spoken to me — let the grandsire hear the fruit of those words.

sanskrit: nyasyāmi śastrāṇi na jātu saṃkhye; pitāmaho drakṣyati māṃ sabhāyām tvayi praśānte tu mama prabhāvaṃ; drakṣyanti sarve bhuvi bhūmipālāḥ
english: I lay down my weapons — never shall the grandsire see me in battle, nor in the assembly hall; but when you are at peace, all the kings on earth shall witness my power.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ity evam uktvā sa mahādhanuṣmān; hitvā sabhāṃ svaṃ bhavanaṃ jagāma bhīṣmas tu duryodhanam eva rājan; madhye kurūṇāṃ prahasann uvāca
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, that great bowman left the assembly hall and went to his own dwelling. Then Bhīṣma, O king, laughing, spoke to Duryodhana alone in the midst of the Kauravas.

sanskrit: satyapratijñaḥ kila sūtaputras; tathā sa bhāraṃ viṣaheta kasmāt vyūhaṃ prativyūhya śirāṃsi bhittvā; lokakṣayaṃ paśyata bhīmasenāt
english: 'The son of the charioteer is said to be true to his vow — then why can he not bear that burden? Counter his battle-array, cleave open skulls, and behold the destruction of the world from Bhīmasena!'

sanskrit: āvantyakāliṅgajayadratheṣu; vedidhvaje tiṣṭhati bāhlike ca ahaṃ haniṣyāmi sadā pareṣāṃ; sahasraśaś cāyutaśaś ca yodhān
english: 'When the Avantis, Kaliṅgas, Jayadratha, Vedadhvaja, and Bāhlika stand firm, I shall always slay thousands upon tens of thousands of the enemy's warriors.'

sanskrit: yadaiva rāme bhagavaty anindye; brahma bruvāṇaḥ kṛtavāṃs tad astram tadaiva dharmaś ca tapaś ca naṣṭaṃ; vaikartanasyādhamapūruṣasya
english: 'From the very moment that the son of Vikartana, that basest of men, falsely claiming brahminhood, obtained that weapon from the blessed and blameless Rāma — from that very moment his dharma and his austerities were destroyed.'

sanskrit: athoktavākye nṛpatau tu bhīṣme; nikṣipya śastrāṇi gate ca karṇe vaicitravīryasya suto 'lpabuddhir; duryodhanaḥ śāṃtanavaṃ babhāṣe
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, after Bhīṣma had spoken to the king and Karṇa had laid down his weapons and departed, Duryodhana, the dim-witted son of Vicitravīrya's son, spoke to the son of Shantanu.

sanskrit: duryodhana uvāca sadṛśānāṃ manuṣyeṣu sarveṣāṃ tulyajanmanām katham ekāntatas teṣāṃ pārthānāṃ manyase jayam
english: Duryodhana said: Among all men who are equal and of the same birth, how can you believe that victory belongs exclusively to those Pāṇḍavas?

sanskrit: sarve sma samajātīyāḥ sarve mānuṣayonayaḥ pitāmaha vijānīṣe pārtheṣu vijayaṃ katham
english: We are all of the same lineage, all born of human wombs — O grandsire, how do you foresee victory for the sons of Pāṇḍu?

sanskrit: nāhaṃ bhavati na droṇe na kṛpe na ca bāhlike anyeṣu ca narendreṣu parākramya samārabhe
english: I do not undertake this enterprise relying on you, nor on Droṇa, nor on Kṛpa, nor on Bāhlika, nor on any other foremost kings.

sanskrit: ahaṃ vaikartanaḥ karṇo bhrātā duḥśāsanaś ca me pāṇḍavān samare pañca haniṣyāmaḥ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: I, Karṇa the son of Vikartana, and my brother Duḥśāsana — we three shall slay the five Pāṇḍavas in battle with sharp arrows.

sanskrit: tato rājan mahāyajñair vividhair bhūridakṣiṇaiḥ brāhmaṇāṃs tarpayiṣyāmi gobhir aśvair dhanena ca
english: After that, O king, with great sacrifices of various kinds and immense gifts, I shall gratify the brahmanas with cows, horses, and wealth.

sanskrit: vidura uvāca śakunīnām ihārthāya pāśaṃ bhūmāv ayojayat kaś cic chākunikas tāta pūrveṣām iti śuśruma
english: Vidura said: O dear one, we have heard that a certain fowler of old spread a snare on the ground for the purpose of catching birds.

sanskrit: tasmin dvau śakunau baddhau yugapat samapauruṣau tāv upādāya taṃ pāśaṃ jagmatuḥ khacarāv ubhau
english: In that snare two birds of equal strength were caught simultaneously; picking up that snare, both of those sky-goers flew away.

sanskrit: tau vihāyasam ākrāntau dṛṣṭvā śākunikas tadā anvadhāvad anirviṇṇo yena yena sma gacchataḥ
english: Seeing those two having taken to the sky, the fowler then chased after them persistently, following wherever they went.

sanskrit: tathā tam anudhāvantaṃ mṛgayuṃ śakunārthinam āśramastho muniḥ kaś cid dadarśātha kṛtāhnikaḥ
english: Then a certain sage who had completed his daily rites and was dwelling in his hermitage saw that hunter running thus after the birds he desired.

sanskrit: tāv antarikṣagau śīghram anuyāntaṃ mahīcaram ślokenānena kauravya papraccha sa munis tadā
english: O Kauravya, the sage then questioned that earth-dweller who was swiftly pursuing those two who moved through the sky, with this verse:

sanskrit: vicitram idam āścaryaṃ mṛgahan pratibhāti me plavamānau hi khacarau padātir anudhāvasi
english: 'This strikes me as a remarkable wonder, O hunter — you are pursuing on foot two birds that fly and soar through the air!'

sanskrit: śākunika uvāca pāśam ekam ubhāv etau sahitau harato mama yatra vai vivadiṣyete tatra me vaśam eṣyataḥ
english: The fowler said: 'Both of these birds together are carrying off my single snare; wherever they quarrel with each other, there they shall fall into my power.'

sanskrit: vidura uvāca tau vivādam anuprāptau śakunau mṛtyusaṃdhitau vigṛhya ca sudurbuddhī pṛthivyāṃ saṃnipetatuḥ
english: Vidura said: Those two birds, having come to quarrel, bound together by the snare of death, grappling with each other in their utter foolishness, fell to the ground.

sanskrit: tau yudhyamānau saṃrabdhau mṛtyupāśavaśānugau upasṛtyāparijñāto jagrāha mṛgayus tadā
english: Then, as those two fought furiously, led by the noose of death, the hunter approached undetected and seized them both.
